title: Real-world GCP Workflow Overview
content: In this final chapter, we'll walk through a realistic workflow: from setting up your project and networking to deploying a multi-tier application with CI/CD and monitoring.
insight: Building in the cloud is about connecting services to create a robust and scalable system.

lab.command: gcloud projects list --limit=1

title: Defining the Resource Hierarchy
content: Start by creating a new project for your application. This ensures isolation from other workloads and allows for clean billing and access control.
insight: Use a consistent naming convention for your projects, such as [org]-[app]-[env].

lab.command: gcloud projects create ace-workflow-prod --name='ACE Workflow Production'

title: Creating the Custom VPC
content: Create a custom-mode VPC network to have full control over your subnet ranges and regions.
insight: Avoid the 'default' VPC for production workloads to maintain a clean security posture.

lab.command: gcloud compute networks create app-vpc --subnet-mode=custom

title: Designing Subnets for Tiers
content: Create separate subnets for your web tier and database tier. This allows you to apply different security policies to each tier.
insight: Place your database in a private subnet without an external IP address.

lab.command: gcloud compute networks subnets create web-subnet --network=app-vpc --region=us-central1 --range=10.0.1.0/24

title: Hardening with Firewall Rules
content: Create firewall rules that allow only necessary traffic. For example, allow HTTP/HTTPS to the web tier and only allow traffic from the web tier to the database tier.
insight: Use network tags or service accounts as the source/target for your rules for better maintainability.

lab.command: gcloud compute firewall-rules create allow-lb-to-web --network=app-vpc --allow=tcp:8080 --source-ranges=130.211.0.0/22,35.191.0.0/16 --target-tags=web-server

title: Reserving Front-end IPs
content: Reserve a global static IP address for your application's load balancer. This provides a stable entry point for your users.
insight: You'll point your domain name's A record to this IP address.

lab.command: gcloud compute addresses create lb-ip --global

title: Creating Tier-specific Service Accounts
content: Create separate service accounts for each component of your application. For example, 'web-sa' and 'db-sa'.
insight: Service accounts represent the 'identity' of your code, not the users.

lab.command: gcloud iam service-accounts create web-sa --display-name='Web Tier Service Account'

title: Applying Least Privilege
content: Grant each service account only the roles it needs. 'web-sa' might need access to a specific Cloud Storage bucket, while 'db-sa' needs access to Cloud SQL.
insight: Never use the default Compute Engine service account for your production workloads.

lab.command: gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding ace-workflow-prod --member='serviceAccount:web-sa@ace-workflow-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role='roles/logging.logWriter'

title: Setting up Artifact Registry
content: Create a Docker repository in Artifact Registry to store your application's container images.
insight: Use regional repositories to reduce latency and egress costs during deployments.

lab.command: gcloud artifacts repositories create app-repo --repository-format=docker --location=us-central1

title: Deploying Cloud SQL
content: Create a managed Cloud SQL instance for your database. Use Private IP to ensure the database is not accessible from the internet.
insight: Managed databases handle backups, patching, and failover for you.

lab.command: gcloud beta sql instances create app-db --database-version=POSTGRES_15 --tier=db-f1-micro --region=us-central1 --network=app-vpc --no-assign-ip

title: Securing Credentials in Secret Manager
content: Store your database password and other sensitive information in Secret Manager instead of hardcoding them in your application or config files.
insight: Secrets are versioned and can be rotated without redeploying your entire application.

lab.command: gcloud secrets create db-password --replication-policy=automatic && echo -n 'my-secret-pass' | gcloud secrets versions add db-password --data-file=-

title: Automating with Cloud Build
content: Create a 'cloudbuild.yaml' file that defines the steps to build your Docker image and push it to Artifact Registry.
insight: Cloud Build runs your builds in a secure, isolated environment.

lab.command:
echo 'steps:
- name: gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker
  args: [build, -t, us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT_ID/app-repo/web-app:$COMMIT_SHA, .]
- name: gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker
  args: [push, us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT_ID/app-repo/web-app:$COMMIT_SHA]' > cloudbuild.yaml

title: Linking Source Control
content: Create a trigger in Cloud Build that connects to your GitHub or GitLab repository. The build will start automatically whenever you push new code.
insight: This is the 'Continuous Integration' part of your pipeline.

lab.command: echo 'Create trigger via Cloud Build -> Triggers'
lab.output: Create trigger via Cloud Build -> Triggers

title: Deploying to GKE Autopilot
content: Create a GKE Autopilot cluster for a hands-off, secure, and cost-effective way to run your containerized application.
insight: Autopilot manages the nodes and security configuration for you, following best practices.

lab.command: gcloud container clusters create-auto app-cluster --region=us-central1

title: Connecting GKE to GCP Services
content: Use Workload Identity to allow your GKE Pods to securely access other GCP services like Cloud SQL or Secret Manager.
insight: This eliminates the need to manage long-lived service account keys inside your cluster.

lab.command: echo 'Enable Workload Identity and bind Kubernetes SA to GCP SA'
lab.output: Enable Workload Identity and bind Kubernetes SA to GCP SA

title: Defining Kubernetes Manifests
content: Create a Deployment manifest to run your application and a Service manifest to expose it internally within the cluster.
insight: Use environment variables to pass configuration to your containers.

lab.command:
echo 'apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
...' > deployment.yaml

title: Deploying the Application
content: Use 'kubectl apply' to deploy your application to the GKE cluster. Kubernetes will ensure that the desired number of Pods are running.
insight: Use 'kubectl get pods' to monitor the progress of your deployment.

lab.command: kubectl apply -f deployment.yaml

title: Configuring Global Load Balancing
content: Create an Ingress resource to set up a Global HTTP(S) Load Balancer. This will route external traffic to your GKE service.
insight: The Ingress resource also handles SSL/TLS termination using managed certificates.

lab.command:
echo 'apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: app-ingress
...' > ingress.yaml

title: Enabling HTTPS with Managed Certificates
content: Google can automatically provision and renew SSL certificates for your domain. Simply create a ManagedCertificate resource and reference it in your Ingress.
insight: Encrypting all traffic is essential for modern web security.

lab.command:
echo 'apiVersion: networking.gke.io/v1
kind: ManagedCertificate
metadata:
  name: app-cert
spec:
  domains:
    - myapp.example.com' > certificate.yaml

title: Point-to-IP with Cloud DNS
content: Update your Cloud DNS managed zone to point your domain name to the static IP address of the load balancer.
insight: Your application is now accessible to the world via your custom domain.

lab.command: gcloud dns record-sets transaction start --zone=my-zone && gcloud dns record-sets transaction add --zone=my-zone --name='myapp.example.com.' --type=A --ttl=300 '34.120.x.x' && gcloud dns record-sets transaction execute --zone=my-zone

title: Defining Readiness and Liveness Probes
content: Configure health checks in your Kubernetes manifests. Liveness probes check if your container is running; readiness probes check if it's ready to handle traffic.
insight: Probes prevent Kubernetes from sending traffic to a Pod that is still starting up or has crashed.

lab.command:
echo 'livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /healthz
    port: 8080' >> deployment.yaml

title: Centralizing Logs
content: Ensure all your application tiers are sending logs to Cloud Logging. This provides a unified view for troubleshooting across your entire system.
insight: In GKE, anything written to stdout or stderr is automatically captured by Cloud Logging.

lab.command: gcloud logging read 'resource.type=k8s_container' --limit=1

title: Visualizing Health with Dashboards
content: Create a custom Cloud Monitoring dashboard to track key metrics like request latency, error rates, and resource utilization for all your tiers.
insight: A good dashboard allows you to see the health of your system at a glance.

lab.command: echo 'Create custom dashboard in Monitoring -> Dashboards'
lab.output: Create custom dashboard in Monitoring -> Dashboards

title: Verifying External Availability
content: Configure a Cloud Monitoring uptime check to periodically verify that your application is reachable from different regions globally.
insight: Uptime checks tell you if your application is 'up' from the perspective of your users.

lab.command: echo 'Configure uptime check for https://myapp.example.com'

title: Responding to Issues with Alerts
content: Create alerting policies to notify your team via Slack or Email if the uptime check fails or if error rates exceed a certain threshold.
insight: Alerts allow you to respond to issues before they significantly impact your users.

lab.command: echo 'Setup alert policy in Monitoring -> Alerting'
lab.output: Setup alert policy in Monitoring -> Alerting

title: Scaling Automatically
content: Enable Horizontal Pod Auto-scaling (HPA) to automatically increase the number of replicas as traffic increases, ensuring consistent performance.
insight: HPA helps you handle traffic spikes efficiently and cost-effectively.

lab.command: kubectl autoscale deployment web-app --cpu-percent=70 --min=2 --max=20

title: Using Infrastructure as Code (IaC)
content: Instead of using the CLI or Console for everything, use tools like Terraform or Cloud Deployment Manager to define your infrastructure in code.
insight: IaC ensures that your environment is reproducible, versioned, and easily shared.

lab.command: echo 'Define VPC, Subnets, and GKE in Terraform (.tf files)'
lab.output: Define VPC, Subnets, and GKE in Terraform (.tf files)

title: Safe Updates with Rolling Strategy
content: When deploying a new version of your app, Kubernetes performs a rolling update, replacing old Pods with new ones one by one to avoid downtime.
insight: You can control the speed and safety of the update using 'maxUnavailable' and 'maxSurge' settings.

lab.command: kubectl set image deployment/web-app web-app=us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/my-project/app-repo/web-app:v2

title: Rolling Back Changes
content: If a new deployment has issues, you can instantly roll back to a previous healthy version using 'kubectl rollout undo'.
insight: Rollbacks are a critical safety net for production environments.

lab.command: kubectl rollout undo deployment/web-app

title: Optimizing Costs
content: Use the Billing dashboard and reports to monitor your cloud spend. Export your billing data to BigQuery for deep analysis.
insight: Cost optimization is a continuous process of rightsizing resources and deleting unused ones.

lab.command: echo 'Check Billing -> Reports for spend breakdown'
lab.output: Check Billing -> Reports for spend breakdown

title: Protecting with Cloud Armor
content: Add a Cloud Armor security policy to your load balancer to protect against common web attacks and block malicious traffic.
insight: Layer 7 security is essential for any public-facing application.

lab.command: gcloud compute security-policies create protect-app --description='Policy for web-app'

title: Accelerating with Cloud CDN
content: Enable Cloud CDN on your load balancer's backend service to cache static assets at the edge, reducing latency for your users.
insight: CDN also reduces egress costs and decreases the load on your origin servers.

lab.command: gcloud compute backend-services update web-backend --global --enable-cdn

title: Enforcing Trust with Binary Authorization
content: Configure Binary Authorization to ensure that only images signed by your Cloud Build pipeline can be deployed to the production GKE cluster.
insight: Prevents the deployment of unauthorized or tampered container images.

lab.command: echo 'Enable Binary Authorization and configure attestors'
lab.output: Enable Binary Authorization and configure attestors

title: Auditing Traffic with VPC Flow Logs
content: Enable VPC flow logs on your subnets to record all network traffic. Use these logs for auditing, security analysis, and troubleshooting connectivity.
insight: Flow logs provide deep visibility into how your microservices are communicating.

lab.command: gcloud compute networks subnets update web-subnet --region=us-central1 --enable-flow-logs

title: Disaster Recovery Planning
content: Simulate failures (e.g., a zone outage or a database crash) to test your recovery procedures and ensure your RPO and RTO are met.
insight: A disaster recovery plan is only as good as its last successful test.

lab.command: echo 'Perform chaos engineering tests on dev/staging environment'
lab.output: Perform chaos engineering tests on dev/staging environment

title: Exporting Logs for Compliance
content: Create a log sink to export your audit and application logs to Cloud Storage for long-term retention and compliance requirements.
insight: GCS is a very cost-effective way to store large volumes of historical log data.

lab.command: gcloud logging sinks create archive-sink storage.googleapis.com/projects/my-project/buckets/audit-logs --log-filter='severity>=INFO'

title: Alerting on Critical Log Events
content: Create log-based metrics and alerts for specific application-level events, such as 'successful payment' or 'failed login attempt'.
insight: Log-based alerts provide insights that standard infrastructure metrics can't capture.

lab.command: echo 'Create log-based metric for "authentication failed"'

title: Regular Security Audits
content: Use Security Command Center and IAM Recommender to perform regular audits of your environment and identify potential risks.
insight: Security is not a one-time setup, but a continuous cycle of improvement.

lab.command: echo 'Review SCC findings and IAM recommendations'
lab.output: Review SCC findings and IAM recommendations

title: The Lifecycle of a Cloud Engineer
content: You have now seen the full lifecycle of a cloud application: Design, Build, Deploy, Operate, and Secure. Each step is critical for success.
insight: Continuous learning and automation are the hallmarks of a great Cloud Engineer.

lab.command: gcloud info --format='value(config.project)'

title: Conclusion: Your GCP ACE Journey
content: Congratulations! You have completed the GCP ACE handbook. You are now equipped with the knowledge and practical skills to build and manage professional workloads on Google Cloud.
insight: The real journey begins now. Go forth and build amazing things in the cloud!

lab.command: echo 'GCP ACE Module Completed. Well done!'
lab.output: GCP ACE Module Completed. Well done!
